request: Use the code review preset. Should we merge this pull request that adds profile picture upload to our web app's account settings?
facts: A merged pull request can be reverted cleanly.
The upload works on the intended path: the tests for JPEG and PNG uploads, size limits and the preview all pass.

The new endpoint builds the storage path from the uploaded file name without cleaning it, so a logged-in user who sends a name such as ../../config/settings.py can overwrite any file the server process can write.
The code follows the team's conventions, and both reviewers said it is easy to read and change.
note: Code-review preset named in the request, designed with a serious objection: two approvals, but rejected as critical. MELCHIOR-1 (correctness on the intended path): fact 2, so approve. BALTHASAR-2 (off the intended path): fact 3, a path traversal that lets any user overwrite server files, a security hole under the critical criteria, so reject. CASPER-3 (the colleague who reads it): fact 4, so approve. Fact 1 makes a normal grade at framing possible, so a grade objection citing fact 3 is the way to critical; framing it critical from the start is also right.
